web.title: Installing the Fix for an Exploited WordPress Flaw Can Expose Some Sites One Last Time
web.description: Some WordPress sites can still be attacked while they install the fix for an actively exploited flaw, according to Umut Bayram, the Picus Security researcher who found it.   The update that installs the fix still unpacks its files using the site's old, unpatched code, so an attacker who strikes at the right moment can run code on the server. The researcher advises blocking web access to the site's wp-content/upgrade folder before updating.   The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-119977 , affects WordPress 4.7 through 7.1.3. During a core update that uses a complete package, WordPress unpacks a copy of the new version into a temporary folder inside wp-content/upgrade. That copy includes the WordPress installer, and the web server can usually reach it.   An attacker with no account who can determine the folder's name and access the installer before WordPress deletes the copy can end up running code on the server. web.description: A fix for CVE-2026-83844 , a remote code execution flaw in Windows Paint, is now in the Microsoft Store. Paint gets this fix only through a Store update, not through Windows updates.   The fixed build, 11.2609.401.0, was the newest Paint build in all ten countries The Hacker News checked today. web.title: Malicious Browser Extensions Could Use Claude Dispatch to Run Code on Users' Computers
web.description: A browser extension that can run scripts on claude.ai could make Claude Desktop run code on a person's computer, researchers at Forever Security, an endpoint security company, showed in a test.   The attack needs Dispatch , a Claude feature that lets people send tasks from their phone to Claude Desktop. The flaw that makes this possible can still be exploited, the researchers said earlier this week.   Claude Desktop is an AI agent that can run commands on the computer where it is installed. web.title: Hackers Hide Linux Backdoor in Control Web Panel Server to Execute Commands Without Logs
web.description: A backdoor has been found hiding in the web server that runs Control Web Panel  (CWP), a free panel for managing Linux hosting servers, researchers at QiAnXin's XLab said this week.   The backdoored web server executes commands that attackers send via web requests, and those requests never appear in its access logs.
